items.title: John Casimir Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: How long did you take lessons from Jim Humphrey? About five years.

ctx.x: Well, who did you have in the young tuxedo when you first organized it?

First I could play with him. Mm-hmm. I had a, a platonic called Page on the studio for him. And Albert Jackson on the trombone. Mm-hmm. I had Joe Avery on the trombone. Mm-hmm. And my cousin was alto sax timbres. Mm-hmm. I had a little Jim on the bass drum. I was using a Latinx's piece. Oh, my kid, I used no smear, you know. Oh, my kid, he's very terrific. I like to have a young tuxedo thing. That's right. Right. Right. And then they had the two lads. Yeah. Right. Right. Right. Right. Right. Right. Right. Right.…
Didn't have a baritone or an offer?

items.title: John Casimir Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Old man Humphrey used to teach the bandies.

ctx.x: When did he die? Or is he still alive? My daddy died around 1931. And how old was he when he died? He was 54 years old. Uh huh. 54. Was he an ear man or a reader or both? No, he was playing a band. He was a player. But he didn't fake it all? No, he was reading them 6-8-Modges. Oh yeah, that's it.
Old man Humphrey used to teach the bandies.

Which Humphrey is that? It went out for him grab call. I had to take letters from the grab call. Oh yeah, you mentioned that. Is that Jim Humphrey? The old man Jim Humphrey. Oh yeah. If you want to stop at any time we can't have a phone lines or anything. We can't. Okay. Okay. You see that a lot of people playing music? Uh huh.
